# ApexYard: full content

> Your agents write the code. Your process decides what merges.

This file holds the page content of https://apexyard.ai/ in one file.
It is written in plain words. It gives no prices.
For prices and plan details, read https://apexyard.ai/pricing.

---

# What ApexYard is

ApexYard gives your agents a team's process. Then it checks every pull request against that process.

ApexYard has three products: Build, Gate and Readiness.
Keel is the shared layer under them.

| Name | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| Build | The open-source framework. It guides your agents. |
| Gate | Checks each pull request against your process. |
| Readiness | Measures each repository. |
| Keel | Your team's rules and context, read by every agent. |

## One process, three places

You write a rule one time. Then the rule works in three places:

1. Build guides your agent with the rule.
2. Gate checks each pull request against the rule.
3. Readiness measures the whole repository against the rule.

A miss becomes a new rule. Then the loop starts again.

Example: the rule says "Every change starts from a ticket."
Build makes the agent open a ticket before it writes code.
Gate blocks a pull request with no ticket.
Readiness flags repositories where changes skip tickets.

## Works with

Build works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and omp.

---

# Build (https://apexyard.ai/build)

Build is the open-source framework. Your agents plan before they code. Every change meets a reviewer before it leaves your machine.

Build is for founders and engineering leads who want agent speed and a real process.

## What Build does

- It turns an idea into a spec, a plan and small tickets. A person signs off each step.
- It adds reviewer roles. Code, security, architecture and QA reviewers each check what they know best. They say what to fix.
- It works with an existing repository or a new one. For an existing repository, it adds handbooks and agent guidance in place. For a new product, you start from an empty folder.
- It runs on your machine. The framework and the command line run where your developers already work.

## Licence and cost

- Build is open source under the MIT licence.
- Rules, roles, handbooks and hooks are plain files. You can read them, change them or remove them.
- Build needs no account and no dashboard.

## Install

The hooks are Bash scripts. On macOS and Linux, Bash is there already. On Windows, use Git Bash or WSL.

1. Fork https://github.com/me2resh/apexyard into your organisation on GitHub.
2. Install jq.
3. Clone your fork.
4. Run `bash bin/apexyard doctor`.
5. Open your agent tool in the folder and run `/setup`.

The install guide is at https://apexyard.ai/docs.

## How Build connects to Gate

The ticket, the decision record and the review that your agents make in Build are what Gate checks on GitHub.

---

# Gate (https://apexyard.ai/gate)

Gate checks each pull request against your process. Every merge leaves a record: what was checked, who approved it and the exact commit.

Gate is for engineering leads whose teams merge code that agents wrote.

## What Gate does

- It puts the result in the checks of the pull request. The result shows what passed, what is missing and the next step.
- It checks four things: a linked ticket, a decision record, a review and a named approval.
- An agent never approves its own work. With named approval set up, the merge waits for a person that your team named.
- You can export the record of each merge for an auditor.
- It shows every open change on one screen. You see what each pull request is missing and who holds it up.
- The organisation view shows which pull requests skipped a step, in every repository.

Gate blocks a merge only when you make the check required in GitHub.

## What the GitHub App can see

The App never reads your code. It has no Contents permission. From each pull request it takes the names of the changed files and nothing else.

- Pull requests: read. Titles, descriptions, reviews and the list of changed files.
- Checks: write. The App posts the ApexYard check on each pull request.
- Metadata: read. Repository names, and who can write to each repository.
- Members: read. The App confirms who can manage your organisation when you sign in.

You can remove the App at any time.

## How Gate connects to Build

Gate checks the ticket, the decision record and the review that your agents make in Build.

---

# Readiness (https://apexyard.ai/readiness)

Readiness measures each repository. It tells you if the repository is ready for production, area by area.

Readiness is for CTOs and engineering leads who answer for what ships.

## What Readiness does

Readiness runs one audit on a repository. The audit has ten areas:

- security
- accessibility
- compliance
- analytics
- search
- AI search
- performance
- monitoring
- documentation
- behaviour quality

You get a go or no-go, the gaps in each area and the top actions.

## How Readiness connects to Build

Turn a finding into a rule. Your agents pick up the rule on their next ticket in Build.

---

# Keel

Keel is the name for your team's rules and context. Every agent reads it.

The rules that you write one time live in Keel. Build uses them to guide your agents. Gate uses them to check pull requests. Readiness uses them to measure repositories.
